sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844/ CR / 18 / 2021-22 dated 05.03.2024 pertaining to Survey A.P. No.21/2024 No.196/2 measuring 5960 Square Meters of Madivala village, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Urban District.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 5960 Square Meters in Survey No.196/2 of Madivala village, Anekal Taluk has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.
The respondent No.3 has passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.4,44,41,886/- in respect of 5960 Square Meters, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 17.08.2021 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5 crores per acre.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 /
CR / 18 / 2021-22 dated 05.03.2024.
A.P. No.21/2024 .4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
Further, the respondent No.2 has failed to distinguish between the lands near main road and assumed it to be abutting NH which is completely erroneous.

The respondent No.2 with an intention to help the respondent No.1 has created statements which do not National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49212741/
2 form a part of the pleadings.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 has dealt with a matter which was beyond the submission to the Arbitration and clearly coming within the purview of Section 34(2)(iv) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the respondent No.1 in his claim petition A.P. No.21/2024 had alleged that he was entitled to 50%
addition since guidance value provided for the same for lands abutting National Highway which was not awarded by the respondent No.3 and in this regard once again the respondent No.2 has observed that 50% addition was claimed by the respondent No.1 on the ground that the lands acquired for NH which is incorrect wince the respondent No.1 had clearly claimed that he is entitled to 50% addition as the lands were abutting National Highway.
There is a prima-facie error in understanding the special instructions and thus such error has resulted in patent illegality apparent on the fact of the record.

The respondent No.2 makes an attempt to give sanctity to the special instructions under the notification and at the same time, conveniently disregards the classification of lands under the very same notification by awarding the difference amount to suit the needs of the respondent No.1.
The impugned Arbitral Award on the face of it opposed A.P. No.21/2024 to most basic notions of law, morality and justice.

There is no connection between the observation of the respondent No.2 and the methodology adopted by the respondent No.2 for redetermining the market value rendering the impugned award completely arbitrary and illegal.

There is no finding in the entire impugned Arbitral Award about the category of lands and the respondent No.2 has completely relied upon the guidance value notification and the award based on findings of law which is completely incorrect and contrary to the notification itself.
It is pertinent to note that there were several arbitration cases pending for more than a decade, but she chose to give priority to the instant case filed in the year 2021.
The respondent No.2 failed to follow the procedure laid down in Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently the same is liable to be A.P. No.21/2024 set aside under Section 34(2A)
of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 34 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act and thus rending the impugned Arbitral Award opposed to settled position of law on all the three counts.
The Arbitral Award was passed on 05.03.2024.
The certified copy of the Arbitral Award was received by the petitioner on 21.03.2024.

The stipulated period of 3 months commences from 21.03.2024 the petition is filed within 3 months from the date of receipt of the impugned Arbitral Award by the petitioner and hence, the petition is in time.
The requisite Court fee is paid as per the provisions of Karnataka Court Fees and petition Valuation Act.

sentences.text: This Court has jurisdiction to try this petition since the seat of arbitration was Bengaluru city A.P. No.21/2024 and impugned Arbitral Award was passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner Bengaluru Urban District within the jurisdiction of this Court.

Among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49212741/

.6. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?"
.7.
The respondent No.1 filed Objection claiming that the petition is not maintainable either in law, devoid of merits, completely erroneous and hence A.P. No.21/2024 deserves to be set aside.
The respondent No.1 admitted the acquisition of land and passing of the award as claimed in the petition.

The respondent No. 1 in her detailed objection denied the para wise written statements and claimed that the Arbitrator /
respondent No. 2 by appreciating acquired land the material on record properly enhanced the compensation and there is no material placed by the petitioner to interfere with the order of respondent No. 2 and accordingly prayed to dismiss the petition.

Point: Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Smt. Shakuntalamma is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.196/2 measuring to an extent of 5960 Sq. Meters of Madivala village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH- 844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020,
is an admitted fact.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.4,44,41,886/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation in respect of 5960 Square Meters.

.10. In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.

Arbitrator vide order dated 05.03.2024 enhanced the compensation.

The said enhancement is under challenge in this petition with the claim of the petitioner that the LAO has passed the award by following due procedures as contemplated under Sections 26 to 30 along with first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and claims that there is no scope for the Arbitrator to enhance the compensation and the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 ought to have confirmed the award passed by the respondent No.3/
LAO.
.11.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid definite contention, it is just and necessary to see what are the criteria to determine the market value of the acquired land as per new Act has to be considered by this Court.

Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, A.P. No.21/2024 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the land by the Collector, Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of amount of compensation,
Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building.
Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing A.P. No.21/2024 and determining the market value of the land, namely:--
(a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated; or (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:
Provided that the date for determination of market value shall be the date on which the notification has been issued under section 11".

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first A.P.
No.21/2024 schedule.

In view of the aforesaid law and facts, whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act

,
certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in- consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

.12. The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the arbitrator applied 1.5 multiplier though A.P. No.21/2024 the said multiplication is applicable to the land to the extent of only 5 guntas and the said multiplication is not applicable to this case as the extent of property is more than 5 guntas.

The petitioner also claimed that the Arbitrator has added 50% to the market value National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49212741/
6 holding that acquired land is abutting to National Highway but the claim of the petitioner is that it is the newly formed highway on the acquired land and the land of the petitioner is acquired for formation of highway, as such, there is no possibility of abutting highway to the property of respondent No.1.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence question of adding 50% of the market value of the property of the petitioner does not arise.

The petitioner has taken up one more contention is that the market value was determined and fixed, hence special instructions for enhancement of compensation is not applicable to the property of the petitioner.

In view of these contentions the petitioner has to prove that the property of the respondent No.1 has been acquired for formation of new road and value of the property of the A.P. No.21/2024 petitioner had been already declared.

Per contra, the respondent No. 1 has to prove that his property was abutting to the national highway prior to the acquisition of property and he is entitled for enhancement as per the special instructions as the competent authority have not declared the market value of the acquired property.
.13. As per the Gazette notification dated 05.12.2018, 1.5 multiplication is applicable only to the property that will not exceed more than 5 guntas.
The property involved in this case is almost 59 guntas, hence the said multiplication certainly not applicable to the present case on hand.

.14. The petitioner claims that the land involved in this case is acquired for new project and there was no existing highway so that the Arbitrator can add additional 50% of compensation but there is no material such as sketch that shows the identification of property in which the project stated in the petition had been carried out.
Hence the said contention of the petitioner cannot be accepted in this case.
The petitioner during the course of arguments has produced the gazette notification dated 05.12.2018 regarding the fixing of market value / guidance value.
As per the said document, the property involved in this case i.e., property in Sy.No. 196/2 of Madivala village comes under the potential Zone for which value is fixed at Rs. 105 lakhs per acre.
As per condition No. 4, in the guidance value the 50% or respective enhancement of 35, 30 or 25 percent can be added if the guidance value is not fixed.
When the guidance value is fixed, question of adding aforesaid percentages certainly does not arise.
.16. I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the 2nd paragraph at page No. 5 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated about the respective contentions of the parties as well as acquisition of property by issuing notifications and it is simply stated that there is a discrimination in awarding the compensation and it is stated that first some A.P. No.21/2024 claimants the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.
3,088.71 per Square Meter but in this case awarded only Rs. 2347.42 per Square Meter but the entire judgment nowhere discloses for which property and in which case the LAO had awarded compensation at Rs.3,088.71 per Square Meter.
Apart from that what is the nature of property in which the LAO granted compensation of Rs. 3,088.71 per Square Meter.
Even as per the guidance value, there are different rates are fixed for different properties.

Under such circumstances without specifying the cases in which the aforesaid compensation is granted and if the lands in such cases are not equivalent to the property involved in this case certainly the said compensation cannot be awarded.

Therefore, the said reason of LAO for enhancement of compensation of Rs. 741/- per National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49212741/
7 Square Meter as a difference of some other cases cannot be accepted in this case.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Shakuntalamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
.17. The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with A.P.
No.21/2024 Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, it is for the respondent No. 1 to demonstrate that the award passed by the LAO is not accordance with Section 26 to 30 as well as first Schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Even there is no reasoning in the award that the LAO had not followed the aforesaid provisions and even there is no material on record to show that the Arbitrator has gone through the award passed by the LAO and modified or enhanced the compensation.

.18. It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
There is no material on record A.P.
No.21/2024 to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be accepted.

.19. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /
LAO has not awarded the compensation as stated in the aforesaid provision of law.

The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted A.P. No.21/2024 the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.

Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable A.P. No.21/2024 to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.

In the result following:
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.

Therefore, it is for the respondent No. 1 to demonstrate that the award passed by the LAO is not accordance with Section 26 to 30 as well as first Schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
Even there is no reasoning in the award that the LAO had not followed the aforesaid provisions and even there is no material on record to show that the Arbitrator has gone through the award passed by the LAO and modified or enhanced the compensation.
.18. It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
There is no material on record A.P.
No.21/2024 to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.
The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.
When the LAO has granted A.P. No.21/2024 the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.
The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
